title: Adult-reported difficulty meeting household expenses rose from the pre-pandemic baseline to 2025
source_unit: ANU COVID-19 Monitoring Survey Program / ANUPoll, summarized by the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare

denominator.unit: Australian adults responding to the ANUPoll household-expenses question

difficult_meet_expenses.unit: percent finding it difficult or very difficult to meet household expenses

observations.method: ANUPoll repeated survey question summarized in the AIHW income and income inequality report.
observations.uncertainty: The summary does not provide the full 2020 wave sample, weighting, question wording, or subgroup denominator in the accessible page; this is an adult-level perception measure, not a household administrative outcome.
observations.subgroup: Australian adults answering the household-expenses difficulty question.
observations.counterinterpretation: Reported difficulty can reflect expectations, temporary shocks, household composition, or survey mode and does not identify bills, debt, income, or realized consumption.

denominator.unit: Australian adults responding to the ANUPoll household-expenses question

difficult_meet_expenses.unit: percent finding it difficult or very difficult to meet household expenses

observations.method: ANUPoll repeated survey question summarized in the AIHW income and income inequality report; the report describes polls from February 2020 through April 2025.
observations.uncertainty: The accessible summary does not establish individual longitudinal change, causal drivers, exact wave sample, or equivalence with ABS household-level cash-flow questions; the 2025 result is a reported adult survey share.
observations.subgroup: Australian adults answering the household-expenses difficulty question.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher reported difficulty can coexist with employment growth, social reconnection, transfers, savings drawdown, or improved expectations in other domains; it is not a complete household-welfare measure.

related_sources.claim: ANU Data Archive route for ANUPoll datasets and study documentation.
AIHW summary reports the January 2020 and April 2025 adult financial-stress comparison and ANUPoll coverage.

boundary: This record adds an adult-level repeated ANUPoll household-expenses measure to challenge household-level ABS and HILDA evidence. It does not establish causal financial hardship, household prevalence, individual change, or a company effect.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: AIHW income and income inequality page reviewed for ANUPoll coverage, January 2020 baseline, April 2025 estimate, and survey limitations.
